title: Locke Extension — managed policy
description: Enterprise-administrator-controlled settings for the Locke browser extension. Values delivered via chrome.storage.managed (Chrome ExtensionSettings policy / Firefox 3rdparty policy / managed-storage manifest). Where present, managed values override user-local settings.

allowedProviders.description: Catalog provider IDs whose web surfaces this extension may screen. These are the `id` values in shared/ai-surfaces.json that have `web_hosts` — not product nicknames, and not API-endpoint identifiers. An empty array or an unset key means EVERY catalog surface is screened, which is the default. A non-empty list is SUBTRACTIVE: it can only remove surfaces from screening, never add one, because the content scripts are declared against the catalog at build time. Note what narrowing this costs: a surface excluded here is not screened at all, so prompts to it leave the machine unexamined. `search` covers the search engines that carry AI answers (www.google.com, www.bing.com, duckduckgo.com, kagi.com, you.com, search.brave.com); tests/shim.test.js pins this list against the catalog so the two cannot drift.

telemetryEnabled.description: ACCEPTED AND INERT — do not cite it as a control. No runtime code reads this key: background/service-worker.js::handleTelemetry writes its shape-only console.debug line unconditionally, and nothing else consults the value. A policy that sets it is stored and ignored. It is still declared here, and still in MANAGED_KEYS, so a fleet that already pushes it is not rejected; wiring it or removing it is a separate decision. Nothing leaves the device either way. To silence the healthy-path console lines, use debugLogging, which IS enforced.

heartbeatSeconds.description: How often the extension probes the Locke desktop app for health. Lower = faster failure detection, more CPU. Higher = longer recovery time after the desktop app restarts.

debugLogging.description: Whether the capture path prints its normal-path decisions (allow / redact / out-of-scope) to the browser console. Warnings for a blocked or unscreened send are printed regardless of this setting. Shape-only either way: host, path, byte counts, media types and decisions — never request bodies or header values.

enforceTimeoutMs.description: How long the page-side shim holds an outbound AI request waiting for the Locke desktop app's verdict before failing closed and blocking it. Must exceed worst-case screening time on the slowest machine it is deployed to, or healthy sends will be blocked.

lockedSettings.description: ACCEPTED AND INERT — do not cite it as a control. This once described a popup that rendered listed names as read-only with a 'managed by your organisation' hint. There is no such UI: popup/popup.html contains no form controls at all, it only reports connection and screening status, so there is nothing for this key to lock. Nothing reads it. It is still declared here, and still in MANAGED_KEYS, so a fleet that already pushes it is not rejected; wiring it or removing it is a separate decision. Note that managed values already win over local ones wherever a setting IS enforced (DEFAULTS < storage.local < storage.managed), which is the protection this key reads as offering.
